title: Apple Maps Adopts 'Lake America' as MapQuest Soars to No. 1 App
excerpt: Apple followed Google in renaming Lake Ontario after Trump's executive order, while MapQuest's refusal to comply made it the top free iPhone app in the US.
body:
• Apple Maps changed Lake Ontario to "Lake America" for US users on September 1, following Trump's August 27 executive order and a direct ask from the president to Apple.
  • Google Maps made the same change a day earlier; both services show "Lake Ontario" to Canadian users and both names to everyone else.
  • MapQuest refused to adopt the new name and shot to No. 1 on the Apple App Store, overtaking ChatGPT, with app usage roughly 50 times its level a week ago.
  • A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 63% of Americans oppose the renaming, while 57% oppose Trump's new tariffs on Canada — even Republicans lean against the lake name change, 43% to 33%.

Apple has changed the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" on Apple Maps for users in the United States, following President Donald Trump's executive order signed on August 27. The move came after Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said on Fox Business that Trump "reached out to Apple directly" about the change, adding that he expected it to happen soon.

By September 1, the renaming appeared on Apple's web-based Maps and began rolling out on mobile devices, though some users still reported seeing Lake Ontario on Tuesday. Apple has not publicly commented on the change.

Tech Giants Comply, MapQuest Refuses

Google Maps adopted the "Lake America" designation a day earlier, on August 30, citing its long-standing policy of reflecting names from the U.S. Geographic Names Information System. "People using Maps in the U.S. will see 'Lake America,'" Google said. "Those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario,' and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names."

https://x.com/CBSNews/status/2095195633246220589

MapQuest took the opposite approach. On the day of Trump's executive order, the mapping service posted on X: "We're not changing it." The company, which took a similar stance when Trump renamed the Gulf of Mexico to "Gulf of America" in January 2025, also launched a tool letting users name the lake whatever they want.

"We took the same approach we did with the Gulf of Mexico: be part of the conversation, and give people an app that keeps the names they're familiar with."

— Doug Berger, General Manager of MapQuest

The refusal turned into a windfall. MapQuest rose to the No. 1 free app on Apple's App Store by September 1, overtaking ChatGPT and ESPN Fantasy Sports. It reached No. 8 on Google Play. The company said app usage was roughly 50 times higher than a week earlier. Even Eric Trump weighed in on X, quipping: "Shocking to see you're still alive… I thought the iPhone 3 took you out 15 years ago."

Americans Overwhelmingly Oppose the Renaming

A Reuters/Ipsos poll of 1,023 US adults, conducted August 28–30, found 63% oppose the Lake Ontario renaming compared to just 14% who support it. Even among Republicans, opposition outpaced support, 43% to 33%. Strong opponents outnumbered strong supporters roughly 7 to 1.

The same poll found 57% of Americans oppose Trump's new tariffs on Canadian goods, versus 20% in support. Trump imposed 50% tariffs on many Canadian imports after bilateral trade talks collapsed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney retaliated with tariffs of 15% to 50% on US exports.

A Lake Named Before the Province

Trump's executive order directed the Interior Department and the U.S. Board on Geographic Names to formalize the name change within 30 days. The order governs federal naming practices and does not require Canada, state governments, or private companies to adopt the new designation.

The name "Lake Ontario" dates back centuries and derives from the Iroquoian word "oniatarí:io," commonly translated as "lake of shining waters," according to the Center for Great Lakes Literacy. The lake forms part of the US-Canada border as the easternmost of the five Great Lakes, draining through the St. Lawrence River toward the Atlantic Ocean. It was named long before the Canadian province that took its name.

Canadian officials have said they will continue calling the lake by its original name. Prime Minister Carney has maintained that the name remains Lake Ontario for Canada and much of the world — just as most countries, including Mexico, have not adopted "Gulf of America" after Trump's similar order in January 2025.

What Comes Next

The trade war shows no sign of easing. Trump has threatened to double tariffs on Canadian automobiles and auto parts from 25% to 50%. With midterm elections approaching on November 3, the Reuters/Ipsos data suggests the Canada dispute could add to political headwinds for Trump's Republican allies defending slim congressional majorities. The president's approval rating has been at the lowest level of his political career in recent weeks, according to Reuters.
nri_angle: The renaming of Lake Ontario affects the millions of Indian-origin residents in the US and Canada, two of the largest diaspora populations, amid an escalating trade war between the two countries.
